name: Ad Honesty & Provider Contract
note: The build now carries the AdMob SDK. Consent is not optional for the five EEA languages this app ships, so the mutations below break each half of that flow separately: the request for consent, each of the three gated ad paths, and the way back into the choice.

mutations.name: the placeholder provider claims to be a real ad network
mutations.why: Every placement branches on isReal to decide whether to say "watching an ad" or "ad placeholder". A provider that lies here makes all four of them lie at once.

mutations.name: the rewarded ad is requested without checking consent
mutations.why: One deleted guard serves a personalised ad to a player who was never asked. Every other test keeps passing, which is exactly why this is checked in the source rather than left to a device run that happened once.
mutations.expectFailure: runRewarded requests an ad without checking canRequestAds

mutations.name: consent is never requested at all
mutations.why: Without requestConsentInfo the first ad goes out before anyone has been asked. In the EEA that is an advertising policy violation, not a bug.
mutations.expectFailure: init() does not ask the consent SDK

mutations.name: the way back into the consent choice is removed
mutations.why: Google requires a path back for anyone shown the form. Without it the choice is permanent from the player's side.
mutations.expectFailure: never asks whether a privacy options form exists

mutations.name: a fresh install is shown an interstitial on its first win
mutations.why: The shipped defect, restored. The hourly cap compares against the last interstitial, and a fresh install has none: the stored value is absent, read as 0, and now minus 0 is always past an hour. Someone who installed the app met a full-screen ad on the first game they ever won. Removing the grace check brings that back, and the gate must see it by running the service against empty storage — the source of the cap looked correct the whole time.
mutations.expectFailure: A fresh install must not be shown an interstitial

mutations.name: the new-player grace is quietly shortened to an hour
mutations.why: Forty-eight hours is a product decision, taken so a player gets through their first sessions before any interruption. Shrinking the constant still suppresses the very first win and would pass a check that only looked at t=0, which is why the gate probes one minute short of the boundary.

mutations.name: a first-launch time in the future is trusted
mutations.why: If the device clock is moved back after first launch, the stored time sits in the future and now minus it stays negative — the interstitial would be suppressed until that moment plus 48 hours, with no upper bound. The guard replaces a future value with now.

mutations.name: the grace clock is no longer started at launch
mutations.why: canShowInterstitial stamps first-seen too, so without the startup call nothing breaks visibly — the clock simply starts at the first win instead of at install, and a player who took a day to win anything loses that day of grace. Behaviour cannot show this from the service alone, so the gate checks main.jsx, the file that runs once at startup.

mutations.name: the revive button goes silent again when there is no ad
mutations.why: The shipped behaviour: a revive that found no ad changed nothing on screen, indistinguishable from a broken button. During the AdMob review no-fill is common, so this is the case players actually meet.
mutations.expectFailure: GameOverModal.jsx handleWatchAd does not tell the player why nothing happened

mutations.name: the past-day unlock fails without a word
mutations.why: The daily calendar is the third rewarded placement and the easiest to forget, because its waiting overlay simply disappears on failure and the day looks as it did before the tap.
mutations.expectFailure: DailyChallengeScreen.jsx handleUnlockWithAd does not tell the player why nothing happened

mutations.name: a throw on the way to the ad escapes the placement
mutations.why: Every placement sets a watching flag before awaiting and clears it after. A throw between the two leaves the flag set — the same spinner trap as the unsettled promise, by a different road.
mutations.expectFailure: a throw on the way to the ad must come back as a result

mutations.name: closing the ad early is reported as no ad available
mutations.why: Collapsing the two messages tells a player who skipped the ad to try again later, when trying again now and watching to the end would work. The difference is the one thing the player controls.
mutations.expectFailure: closing early is something the player can choose not to do

mutations.name: the post-game ad is requested inside the new-player grace
mutations.why: An ad that can never be shown is still a request, and unfilled-by-us requests lower the match rate the account is judged on.
mutations.expectFailure: An ad was requested inside the 48-hour grace

mutations.name: the hourly cap starts even when no ad was shown
mutations.why: Stamping the cap before checking readiness makes one unloaded win silently cost the player nothing and the app an hour of eligible impressions.
mutations.expectFailure: An ad that was not shown must not start the hourly cap

mutations.name: the victory screen renders under the ad again
mutations.why: The ordering this change introduced: the victory screen waits for the ad sequence. Rendering it on victory alone puts its buttons beneath a live interstitial.

mutations.name: permission to request ads read from the status string
mutations.why: External audit V11. The old assertion was 'no status comparison OR privacyOptionsRequirementStatus === REQUIRED anywhere in the file', and the second half is always true, so this exact line passed. A player who declines personalised ads is OBTAINED with canRequestAds true; this reading serves them nothing.

mutations.name: the status gates a request path instead of the form
mutations.why: A status check placed in front of an ad request is the same hand-rolled permission in a different spot. The status may decide whether the form is shown, and nothing else.
mutations.replace: if (!this.canRequestAds || this.lastInfo?.status === 'REQUIRED') return { rewarded: false, reason: 'unavailable' };
mutations.expectFailure: compared somewhere other than the decision to show
